category: Type II - Character and Paragraph controls, OpenType, styles, type on a path and the Type menu
description: Individual typographic controls and Type menu commands not broken out in 'Selection, Image, Edit and Type operations': every Character and Paragraph panel field with its range and TextItem scripting property, the OpenType submenu, Character/Paragraph Styles, point/paragraph/path/area type, warp styles and the font-management commands.

tools.name: Font family and font style (Character panel)
tools.description: Selects the typeface and its weight/style for the selected characters or the whole type layer. The font menu shows a live preview, a search field that matches on any part of the name, a classification filter (Serif, Sans Serif, Script...), an Adobe Fonts filter, favourites (stars), 'Show similar fonts' and a cloud icon to activate fonts from Adobe Fonts in place. Variable fonts expose their axes in the Properties panel.
tools.usage: Character panel / options bar > Font Family and Font Style menus   |   TextItem.font = "<PostScript name>"

parameters.name: Search field
parameters.description: Type any substring, e.g. 'cond bold'; Up/Down arrows preview fonts on the selected text.

parameters.name: Filter by classification / Adobe Fonts / Favorites / Similar
parameters.description: Icons at the top of the font list.

parameters.name: Font Style
parameters.description: Regular, Italic, Bold... as supplied by the font; Faux styles are separate toggles.

tools.notes: Scripts must use the PostScript name (`app.fonts[i].postScriptName`). Type > Font Preview Size sets the menu preview size. Missing fonts show a yellow warning badge on the layer.

tools.name: Font Size (Character panel)
tools.description: Sets the type size in the unit chosen in Preferences > Units & Rulers > Type (points by default; pixels or mm available). Sizes from 0.01 to 1296 pt are accepted; the field supports math ('12+2') and Ctrl+Shift+> / < change the size by 2 pt from the canvas.
tools.usage: Character panel > Size   |   Ctrl+Shift+. / Ctrl+Shift+, (2 pt steps; add Alt for 10 pt)   |   TextItem.size = UnitValue

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: 0.01-1296 pt (or px/mm per preferences).

tools.example:
app.preferences.typeUnits = TypeUnits.PIXELS;
app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.size = 48;   // 48 px
tools.notes: Point size depends on document resolution when the unit is points: at 72 ppi 1 pt = 1 px. Scaling a type layer with Free Transform changes the size value.

tools.name: Leading (Character panel)
tools.description: The vertical distance between baselines of consecutive lines. Auto sets it to a percentage of the font size (120 % by default, adjustable in Paragraph panel > Justification); any explicit value overrides it. Alt+Up/Down changes leading of the selected text by 2 pt from the canvas.
tools.usage: Character panel > Leading (Auto or value)   |   Alt+Up / Alt+Down   |   TextItem.leading, TextItem.useAutoLeading, TextItem.autoLeadingAmount

parameters.name: Leading
parameters.description: 0-5000 pt; 'Auto' uses autoLeadingAmount % of size.

tools.notes: Leading is a character attribute in Photoshop; the largest leading value in a line wins. The Paragraph panel's Space Before/After is the paragraph-level equivalent.

tools.name: Kerning (Character panel)
tools.description: Adjusts the space between two specific characters. Metrics uses the pair-kerning table built into the font, Optical lets Photoshop compute spacing from glyph shapes (better for mixed fonts or fonts with poor tables), and a numeric value (in 1/1000 em) applies manual kerning at the insertion point. Alt+Left/Right kerns by 20 units from the keyboard.
tools.usage: Character panel > Kerning: Metrics / Optical / value   |   Alt+Left / Alt+Right (add Ctrl for 100 units)   |   TextItem.autoKerning = AutoKernType.METRICS | OPTICAL | MANUAL

parameters.name: Kerning
parameters.description: Metrics, Optical, or -1000 to 10000 (thousandths of an em).

tools.example: Click between the 'A' and 'V' of a headline, press Alt+Left three times to tighten by 60/1000 em.
tools.notes: Manual kerning values are stored per character position; they are lost if the font changes to one without the same glyphs. Tracking applies to a range; kerning to a pair.

tools.name: Tracking (Character panel)
tools.description: Loosens or tightens the spacing uniformly across a selected range of characters (or the whole layer), in 1/1000 em. Used for all-caps headlines (positive tracking), tight display type (negative) and to fix rag; it stacks with kerning.
tools.usage: Character panel > Tracking   |   Alt+Left / Alt+Right with text selected   |   TextItem.tracking

parameters.name: Tracking
parameters.description: -1000 to 10000 (thousandths of an em).

tools.example: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.tracking = 80;   // airy caps
tools.notes: Tracking is applied to the right of each character, so the last character of a line also gains space; centre-aligned text may look off-centre at large values.

tools.name: Vertical Scale and Horizontal Scale (Character panel)
tools.description: Stretch or compress glyphs vertically or horizontally as a percentage of their normal proportions. Useful for fitting a headline into a fixed width without changing size, but heavy scaling distorts stroke weights, so prefer condensed/extended font styles where available.
tools.usage: Character panel > Vertical Scale / Horizontal Scale (%)   |   TextItem.verticalScale, TextItem.horizontalScale

parameters.name: Vertical Scale / Horizontal Scale
parameters.description: 0-1000 %; 100 % is unscaled.

tools.example:
var t = app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem;
t.horizontalScale = 90;   // slightly condensed
tools.notes: Free Transform on a type layer writes into these values as well. Reset with Character panel menu > Reset Character.

tools.name: Baseline Shift (Character panel)
tools.description: Raises or lowers selected characters relative to the baseline of the surrounding text - for manual superscripts, adjusting symbols, or moving type along a path off the path. Shift+Alt+Up/Down changes it by 2 pt from the canvas.
tools.usage: Character panel > Baseline Shift (pt)   |   Shift+Alt+Up / Shift+Alt+Down   |   TextItem.baselineShift

parameters.name: Baseline Shift
parameters.description: -1296 to 1296 pt; positive raises.

tools.example: Select the '2' in 'H2O', set Baseline Shift -4 pt and size 60 % to build a subscript manually.
tools.notes: For type on a path, a positive baseline shift lifts the text above the path; negative places it below (or inside a circle).

tools.name: Text color (Character panel)
tools.description: Fills the selected characters (or the whole layer) with a solid colour chosen from the Color Picker; different characters can have different colours in one layer. For gradients, patterns or images inside text use a clipped layer or a Gradient Overlay layer style instead, which keeps the type editable.
tools.usage: Character panel / options bar > Color swatch   |   TextItem.color = SolidColor

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: Any colour in the document's colour mode; the swatch follows the foreground colour when creating a new layer.

tools.notes: Setting `textItem.color` in a script recolours the entire layer. Type layers with a Color Overlay effect ignore the character colour visually.

tools.name: Faux Bold and Faux Italic (Character panel)
tools.description: Synthesise a heavier or slanted version when the font has no real bold or italic style: Faux Bold thickens the outline, Faux Italic skews it about 12 degrees. Use only as a last resort - the synthetic styles disable warping (Faux Bold), can be rejected by print RIPs, and are ignored when exporting text to SVG/PDF as live type.
tools.usage: Character panel > T (Faux Bold) / T-slanted (Faux Italic) buttons; Ctrl+Shift+B / Ctrl+Shift+I with text selected   |   TextItem.fauxBold, TextItem.fauxItalic
tools.example: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.fauxItalic = true;
tools.notes: Warp Text is unavailable while Faux Bold is on ('Could not complete... because the type layer uses a faux bold style'). Prefer a real Bold/Italic style or a variable font weight axis.

tools.name: All Caps and Small Caps (Character panel)
tools.description: Display the selected text in capitals without retyping it: All Caps substitutes uppercase glyphs; Small Caps uses the font's true small-cap glyphs when it has them (OpenType 'smcp') or synthesises reduced capitals otherwise. The underlying characters are unchanged, so the text remains searchable and can be reverted.
tools.usage: Character panel > TT (All Caps) / Tt (Small Caps); Ctrl+Shift+K / Ctrl+Shift+H   |   TextItem.capitalization = TextCase.NORMAL | ALLCAPS | SMALLCAPS
tools.example: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.capitalization = TextCase.SMALLCAPS;
tools.notes: Synthetic small caps are lighter than the surrounding text; fonts with real small caps (e.g. Minion Pro) look far better. Also see Type > OpenType.

tools.name: Superscript and Subscript (Character panel)
tools.description: Reduce the selected characters to a percentage of the size and shift them above or below the baseline for footnote markers, exponents and chemical formulas. If the font carries OpenType 'sups'/'subs' glyphs, those are used; otherwise the glyphs are scaled synthetically.
tools.usage: Character panel > T superscript / T subscript buttons; Ctrl+Shift+= / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+=
tools.example: Select the '2' in 'E = mc2', press Ctrl+Shift+= to superscript it.
tools.notes: The scale and offset used for synthetic super/subscript are fixed in Photoshop (unlike InDesign) - use size and Baseline Shift manually for custom positions.

tools.name: Underline and Strikethrough (Character panel)
tools.description: Draw a line under (or, for vertical type, left/right of) the selected characters, or through their middle. The line weight and offset follow the font size and cannot be customised; for controllable rules draw a shape layer instead.
tools.usage: Character panel > Underline / Strikethrough buttons; Ctrl+Shift+U / Ctrl+Shift+/   |   TextItem.underline = UnderlineType.UNDERLINEON | UNDERLINELEFT | UNDERLINERIGHT | UNDERLINEOFF; TextItem.strikeThru = StrikeThruType.STRIKEBOX | STRIKEHEIGHT | STRIKEOFF
tools.example:
var t = app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem;
t.underline = UnderlineType.UNDERLINEON;
tools.notes: Underline Left/Right apply only to vertical text. The underline colour matches the text colour.

tools.name: Language and dictionary (Character panel)
tools.description: Assigns a language to the selected characters, which drives spell checking (Edit > Check Spelling), hyphenation rules and OpenType locale-specific forms. Mixed-language documents can carry a different language per range.
tools.usage: Character panel > Language menu (bottom-left)   |   TextItem.language = Language.ENGLISHUSA | GERMAN | FRENCH ...

parameters.name: Language
parameters.description: Any of ~40 dictionaries (English: USA, English: UK, Deutsch, Francais, Espanol, Japanese...).

tools.example: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.language = Language.ENGLISHUK;
tools.notes: Type > Language Options chooses the text engine (Default, East Asian, Middle Eastern and South Asian) that decides which panel options and scripts are available.

tools.name: Text anti-aliasing (Type > Anti-Alias)
tools.description: Chooses how type edges are smoothed when rasterised for display and export: None (aliased, for pixel fonts), Sharp, Crisp, Strong, Smooth, and the OS-matched options Windows LCD / Windows (or Mac LCD / Mac) that mimic browser rendering for web mock-ups. Applies per type layer.
tools.usage: Type > Anti-Alias > None / Sharp / Crisp / Strong / Smooth / Windows LCD / Windows   (also Character panel and options bar menu)   |   TextItem.antiAliasMethod = AntiAlias.NONE | SHARP | CRISP | STRONG | SMOOTH | WINDOWSLCD | WINDOWS | MACLCD | MAC
tools.example: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.antiAliasMethod = AntiAlias.CRISP;
tools.notes: Small UI text usually looks best with Sharp or Crisp; Smooth is right for large display type. None is required for bitmap/pixel-art fonts. Anti-aliasing is baked into Export As output.

tools.name: Paragraph alignment and justification (Paragraph panel)
tools.description: Seven alignment buttons: Left, Center, Right align (available for point and paragraph text) and Justify Last Left, Justify Last Centered, Justify Last Right, Justify All (paragraph text only). Justification stretches word and letter spacing according to the Justification dialog settings.
tools.usage: Paragraph panel > alignment buttons; Ctrl+Shift+L / C / R (align), Ctrl+Shift+J (justify last left), Ctrl+Shift+F (justify all)   |   TextItem.justification = Justification.LEFT | CENTER | RIGHT | LEFTJUSTIFIED | CENTERJUSTIFIED | RIGHTJUSTIFIED | FULLYJUSTIFIED
tools.notes: For vertical type the buttons become Top, Center, Bottom. Alignment of point text is relative to the click point.

tools.name: Indents and paragraph spacing (Paragraph panel)
tools.description: Left Indent, Right Indent and First Line Indent inset the paragraph from the text box, and Space Before / Space After add vertical space between paragraphs without empty lines. A negative First Line Indent with a positive Left Indent creates hanging bullets.
tools.usage: Paragraph panel > Indent Left Margin / Indent Right Margin / Indent First Line / Add Space Before Paragraph / Add Space After Paragraph   |   TextItem.leftIndent, rightIndent, firstLineIndent, spaceBefore, spaceAfter

parameters.name: First Line Indent
parameters.description: -1296 to 1296 pt; negative for hanging indents.

tools.notes: Paragraph attributes apply only to paragraph (box) text and to the paragraph containing the cursor unless all text is selected.

tools.name: Hyphenation settings (Paragraph panel)
tools.description: The Hyphenate checkbox enables automatic hyphenation using the character language, and the Hyphenation... dialog sets the rules: minimum word length, minimum letters before/after the hyphen, maximum consecutive hyphens, the hyphenation zone for unjustified text and whether capitalised words may be broken.
tools.usage: Paragraph panel > Hyphenate; panel menu > Hyphenation...   |   TextItem.hyphenation, hyphenateWordsLongerThan, hyphenateAfterFirst, hyphenateBeforeLast, hyphenLimit, hyphenationZone, hyphenateCapitalWords

parameters.name: Words Longer Than
parameters.description: Minimum letters (default 5).

parameters.name: After First / Before Last
parameters.description: Minimum letters on each side of the hyphen (default 2 / 2).

parameters.name: Hyphen Limit
parameters.description: Maximum consecutive hyphenated lines (0 = unlimited).

parameters.name: Hyphenation Zone
parameters.description: Distance from the right edge within which unjustified text may hyphenate (Single-line Composer only).

parameters.name: Hyphenate Capitalized Words
parameters.description: Allow proper nouns to be broken.

tools.notes: Insert a discretionary hyphen with Ctrl+Shift+- to suggest a break point; a No Break character style prevents breaks in a selection.

tools.name: Justification settings and composers (Paragraph panel)
tools.description: The Justification... dialog sets the Minimum/Desired/Maximum percentages for Word Spacing, Letter Spacing and Glyph Scaling used when justifying, plus the Auto Leading percentage. The panel menu also chooses between the Adobe Single-line Composer (line-by-line breaks, predictable) and the Adobe Every-line Composer (optimises breaks over the whole paragraph for even spacing and fewer hyphens).
tools.usage: Paragraph panel menu > Justification... / Adobe Single-line Composer / Adobe Every-line Composer   |   TextItem.minimumWordSpacing..., desiredGlyphScaling..., autoLeadingAmount, textComposer = TextComposer.ADOBESINGLELINE | ADOBEEVERYLINE

parameters.name: Word Spacing
parameters.description: Min/Desired/Max %, default 80/100/133.

parameters.name: Letter Spacing
parameters.description: Min/Desired/Max %, default 0/0/0.

parameters.name: Glyph Scaling
parameters.description: Min/Desired/Max %, default 100/100/100.

parameters.name: Auto Leading
parameters.description: Percentage of type size used for Auto leading, default 120 %.

tools.example: Paragraph panel menu > Justification...: Word Spacing 85/100/120, Glyph Scaling 98/100/102, then switch to Every-line Composer for a smoother rag.
tools.notes: Roman Hanging Punctuation (panel menu) lets quotes and periods hang outside the margin. East Asian options (Kinsoku, Mojikumi, Burasagari) appear when the East Asian text engine is enabled.

tools.name: Character Styles panel
tools.description: Stores named sets of character attributes (font, size, colour, tracking, OpenType features...) that can be applied to any text selection in one click and updated globally by redefining the style. The panel supports creating a style from the current selection, clearing overrides (the '+' badge), loading styles from another document and saving the current styles as the defaults for new documents.
tools.usage: Window > Character Styles (also Type > Panels > Character Styles Panel); panel menu > New Character Style / Redefine Style / Clear Override / Load Character Styles... / Save Default Type Styles

parameters.name: New Character Style
parameters.description: Creates a style from the current selection's formatting; double-click to edit its Basic, Advanced and OpenType tabs.

parameters.name: Clear Override
parameters.description: Removes local formatting so the text matches the style again.

parameters.name: Redefine Character Style by Merging Override
parameters.description: Push the current local overrides into the style definition.

tools.example:
1. Format a caption (Roboto Light 9 pt, tracking 20).
2. Character Styles panel > New Character Style, name 'caption'.
3. Select other captions, click 'caption'; later change the size in the style and all update.
tools.notes: Styles are stored in the document; use Type > Load/Save Default Type Styles to reuse across files. Not exposed in the ExtendScript DOM (use Action Manager).

tools.name: Paragraph Styles panel
tools.description: Like Character Styles but at paragraph level: a Paragraph Style holds alignment, indents, spacing, hyphenation, composer settings and a full set of character attributes, and applies to whole paragraphs. 'Basic Paragraph' is the default style; new styles can be based on it so changes cascade.
tools.usage: Window > Paragraph Styles; panel menu > New Paragraph Style / Redefine / Clear Override / Load Paragraph Styles... / Save Default Type Styles

parameters.name: Based On
parameters.description: Parent style whose attributes are inherited.

parameters.name: Tabs: Basic Character Formats, Advanced Character Formats, OpenType Features, Indents and Spacing, Composition, Justification, Hyphenation
parameters.description: All attributes a paragraph style can define.

tools.example: Create 'Body' (Source Serif 11/15, Every-line Composer, Hyphenate) and 'Heading' (Based On Body, Bold 18 pt, Space After 6 pt); apply by clicking in a paragraph and choosing the style.
tools.notes: Overrides show a '+'; Alt-click a style to apply it and clear overrides. Styles travel with the PSD.

tools.name: OpenType features (Type > OpenType)
tools.description: Toggles the OpenType layout features a font provides for the selected text: Standard Ligatures, Contextual Alternates, Discretionary Ligatures, Swash, Oldstyle (figures), Stylistic Alternates, Titling Alternates, Ornaments, Ordinals, Fractions, Justification Alternates, plus Japanese 78/Expert/Traditional forms, Proportional Metrics, Kana and Roman Italics for East Asian fonts. The same buttons sit at the bottom of the Character panel; unsupported features are greyed out.
tools.usage: Type > OpenType > <feature>   (Character panel OpenType button row)   |   TextItem.ligatures, alternateLigatures, oldStyle, contextualAlternates (partial DOM coverage)

parameters.name: Standard Ligatures (liga)
parameters.description: fi, fl, ff... replacements; on by default.

parameters.name: Contextual Alternates (calt)
parameters.description: Script-font joins that depend on neighbouring letters.

parameters.name: Discretionary Ligatures (dlig)
parameters.description: Decorative ligatures such as ct, st.

parameters.name: Swash (swsh) / Stylistic Alternates (salt) / Titling Alternates (titl)
parameters.description: Alternate glyph sets.

parameters.name: Oldstyle (onum) / Ordinals (ordn) / Fractions (frac)
parameters.description: Figure styles, 1st/2nd superiors, automatic 1/2 fractions.

parameters.name: Ornaments (ornm)
parameters.description: Font's decorative glyphs.

tools.example: Select '1/2 cup' set in a font with fractions, choose Type > OpenType > Fractions; then select 'Th' in a display face and enable Discretionary Ligatures.
tools.notes: Stylistic Sets (ss01-ss20) and single alternates are chosen through the Glyphs panel or the on-canvas alternate-glyph pop-up (Preferences > Type > Enable Type layer glyph alternates). SVG colour fonts (emoji) work through the Glyphs panel.

tools.name: Point Text and Paragraph Text
tools.description: Photoshop's two text-layer kinds: point text starts at a click and grows in one line (breaks only where you press Enter), while paragraph text lives in a resizable bounding box you drag out and wraps automatically. Type > Convert to Paragraph Text / Convert to Point Text switch between them; the Properties panel shows the box dimensions for paragraph text.
tools.usage: Type tool: click for point text, drag for paragraph text (Alt-drag opens a size dialog)   |   Type > Convert to Paragraph Text / Convert to Point Text   |   TextItem.kind = TextType.POINTTEXT | PARAGRAPHTEXT; TextItem.width/height/position

parameters.name: Bounding box handles
parameters.description: Drag to resize the paragraph box (text reflows); Ctrl-drag to scale the type; an overflow icon (+) in the lower-right handle shows hidden text.

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description: Point text: click point (x, y); paragraph text: top-left of the box.

tools.notes: Converting paragraph text with overflow to point text discards the hidden characters (a warning appears). UXP: `textItem.convertToParagraphText()` / `convertToPointText()` (24.1+).

tools.name: Type on a Path
tools.description: Flows text along any open or closed path drawn with the Pen or shape tools: hover the Type tool over the path until the cursor shows a wavy line and click. The Path Selection tool drags the start/end brackets and the centre marker to reposition the text or flip it to the other side of the path; Baseline Shift lifts it off the path. Photoshop 27.10 adds Dynamic Text so the text reflows automatically when the path or shape is edited.
tools.usage: Draw a path > Horizontal Type Tool (T) > click on the path when the cursor changes > type   |   Path Selection tool (A): drag the I-beam markers to slide or flip

parameters.name: Start / end brackets
parameters.description: Limit where text may flow along the path.

parameters.name: Centre marker / flip
parameters.description: Drag across the path to flip the text to the other side (inside a circle).

parameters.name: Baseline Shift
parameters.description: Offsets text above/below the path.

parameters.name: Dynamic Text (27.10+)
parameters.description: Text bound to a shape or path updates as the geometry changes.

tools.example:
1. Ellipse tool in Path mode: draw a circle.
2. Type tool: click the top of the circle, type 'AROUND THE WORLD', Ctrl+Enter.
3. Path Selection tool: drag the start marker to rotate the text around the circle; set Baseline Shift 6 pt to lift it.
tools.notes: The path stays editable with the Direct Selection tool; the text layer's own path is listed in the Paths panel while the layer is selected. Warp Text cannot be combined with type on a path.

tools.name: Area type (type inside a shape)
tools.description: Creates paragraph text whose bounding area is a closed path instead of a rectangle: click inside a closed path with the Type tool when the cursor shows a dotted circle. Text wraps to the shape's outline, and the shape can be edited afterwards with the Direct Selection tool to reflow the text.
tools.usage: Draw a closed path (Pen or shape tool in Path mode) > Type tool > click inside the path > type

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Any closed path; text follows its interior.

parameters.name: Inset
parameters.description: Use Paragraph panel indents to keep text off the outline.

tools.example: Custom Shape tool (Path mode) > heart shape; Type tool click inside; Type > Paste Lorem Ipsum to fill it.
tools.notes: Convert to a normal box with Type > Convert to Paragraph Text; overflow shows a '+' marker.

tools.name: Warp Text styles reference
tools.description: The fifteen non-destructive warp presets available for type layers (and for Smart Objects via Edit > Transform > Warp): Arc, Arc Lower, Arc Upper, Arch, Bulge, Shell Lower, Shell Upper, Flag, Wave, Fish, Rise, Fisheye, Inflate, Squeeze and Twist, each with Bend and Horizontal/Vertical Distortion sliders and a Horizontal/Vertical orientation switch. The text stays editable after warping.
tools.usage: Type > Warp Text... (or the options-bar warp button)   |   TextItem.warpStyle = WarpStyle.ARC | ARCLOWER | ARCUPPER | ARCH | BULGE | SHELLLOWER | SHELLUPPER | FLAG | WAVE | FISH | RISE | FISHEYE | INFLATE | SQUEEZE | TWIST | NONE; warpBend, warpDirection, warpHorizontalDistortion, warpVerticalDistortion

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: One of the fifteen presets or None.

parameters.name: Horizontal / Vertical
parameters.description: Axis of the warp.

parameters.name: Horizontal Distortion / Vertical Distortion
parameters.description: -100 to 100 % perspective-like skew.

tools.notes: Unavailable when Faux Bold is on or the text is on a path. For free-form mesh warps convert to a Smart Object and use Edit > Transform > Warp with a custom grid.

tools.name: Type > Orientation
tools.description: Switches a type layer between horizontal and vertical text flow without retyping. Vertical orientation stacks Latin characters one per line (rotated upright) and is the normal layout for Japanese/Chinese; use Standard Vertical Roman Alignment in the Character panel to rotate Latin runs sideways instead.
tools.usage: Type > Orientation > Horizontal / Vertical   (also the options-bar toggle)   |   TextItem.direction = Direction.HORIZONTAL | VERTICAL
tools.example: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.direction = Direction.VERTICAL;
tools.notes: Alignment buttons change to Top/Center/Bottom for vertical text. The Vertical Type tool creates vertical layers directly.

tools.name: Type > Language Options and text engines
tools.description: Selects which text engine features are exposed: Default Features (Latin), East Asian Features (adds Tsume, Tate-chu-yoko, Kinsoku, Mojikumi, Burasagari and the Japanese OpenType items) or Middle Eastern and South Asian Features (right-to-left paragraph direction, ligature options, diacritic positioning, Hindi digits). The choice mirrors Preferences > Type > Choose Text Engine Options and affects new type layers.
tools.usage: Type > Language Options > Default Features / East Asian Features / Middle Eastern and South Asian Features
tools.example: Choose Type > Language Options > Middle Eastern and South Asian Features, then in the Paragraph panel click the right-to-left paragraph direction button before typing Arabic.
tools.notes: Switching engines requires re-creating existing type layers to expose the new options. Text shaping of complex scripts relies on the World-Ready composer.

tools.name: Type > Update All Text Layers
tools.description: Re-renders every type layer in the document with the current text engine and installed fonts. Needed after opening files created in older versions or on another OS (type layers may show 'needs update' badges), after installing a missing font, or when fonts were substituted during open.
tools.usage: Type > Update All Text Layers
tools.example: Open a CS-era PSD, install the missing typeface, then choose Type > Update All Text Layers to remove the yellow warning badges.
tools.notes: Updating can subtly re-flow paragraph text if kerning tables changed; check line breaks afterwards.

tools.name: Type > Replace All Missing Fonts and Resolve Missing Fonts
tools.description: Handles type layers whose fonts are not installed: Resolve Missing Fonts opens a dialog listing each missing font with the option to activate it from Adobe Fonts (if available) or substitute a chosen installed font; Replace All Missing Fonts substitutes the default replacement font on every affected layer in one go.
tools.usage: Type > Resolve Missing Fonts...  /  Type > Replace All Missing Fonts

parameters.name: Missing font list
parameters.description: Per font: Activate (Adobe Fonts), Replace with (installed font), or Don't Resolve.

parameters.name: Default replacement
parameters.description: Myriad Pro (Latin) unless changed in the dialog.

tools.example: Open a client PSD; the Missing Fonts dialog appears. Choose Activate for the two Adobe Fonts entries and Replace with 'Inter' for the third.
tools.notes: Layers with missing fonts still render from their cached raster until edited. Resolution is recorded in the PSD once the layer is updated.

tools.name: Type > Paste Lorem Ipsum
tools.description: Fills the active text layer (at the cursor or replacing the selection) with placeholder Latin text so layouts can be judged before final copy exists. Preferences > Type > 'Fill new type layers with placeholder text' automates it for every new paragraph box.
tools.usage: Type > Paste Lorem Ipsum   (with a text layer in edit mode)
tools.example: Drag a paragraph box with the Type tool, then Type > Paste Lorem Ipsum; press Ctrl+Enter to commit.
tools.notes: Only works while editing text. The placeholder is regular text and must be replaced before delivery.

tools.name: Adobe Fonts activation (Type > More from Adobe Fonts)
tools.description: Opens the Adobe Fonts website filtered for Photoshop, and the font menu's cloud icon lets you activate any Adobe Fonts family without leaving the app. Activated fonts sync through Creative Cloud Desktop to every application; missing Adobe Fonts in opened documents are auto-activated when 'Enable Adobe Fonts auto-activation' is on in the Creative Cloud app.
tools.usage: Type > More from Adobe Fonts...   /   Font menu > filter 'Adobe Fonts' > cloud icon > Activate
tools.example: In the Character panel font list, tick the Adobe Fonts filter icon, type 'Source Serif', click the cloud icon to activate and use it immediately.
tools.notes: Requires a signed-in Creative Cloud subscription; activated fonts are not installed as system fonts and cannot be embedded in files sent to non-subscribers.

tools.name: Type > Load Default Type Styles and Save Default Type Styles
tools.description: Save Default Type Styles writes the current Character and Paragraph styles as the defaults loaded into every new document; Load Default Type Styles brings those defaults into the current document. Handy for house style consistency across a team when combined with a shared preferences setup.
tools.usage: Type > Load Default Type Styles  /  Type > Save Default Type Styles
tools.example: Set up 'Body', 'H1' and 'Caption' paragraph styles in a template PSD, then Type > Save Default Type Styles; every File > New now contains them.
tools.notes: Defaults are stored in the user preferences folder, not the document.

tools.name: Type tool options bar
tools.description: The options bar for the Type tools exposes orientation toggle, font family/style/size, anti-aliasing, alignment, colour, the Warp Text button, the toggle for the Character/Paragraph panels and the Cancel (Esc) / Commit (Ctrl+Enter or the tick) controls. Tool presets store a complete type setup for reuse.
tools.usage: Select Horizontal Type Tool (T) > options bar   |   Ctrl+Enter commits, Esc cancels editing

parameters.name: Toggle text orientation
parameters.description: Horizontal/Vertical.

parameters.description: Shows/hides the docked type panels.

tools.example: Press T, set 'Inter Semi Bold 32 pt, Crisp, Center' in the options bar, click the canvas, type, Ctrl+Enter.
tools.notes: While in text-edit mode most shortcuts type characters; commit first. Ctrl-dragging a type layer's box on canvas scales it (Free Transform).

tools.name: Edit > Check Spelling and Find and Replace Text
tools.description: Spell checks type layers against the dictionary chosen per character (Character panel > Language), with Ignore/Change/Add options and an 'all layers' checkbox; Find and Replace Text searches and replaces strings across the current or all type layers with case and whole-word options. Both are also useful for bulk-updating template documents.
tools.usage: Edit > Check Spelling...  /  Edit > Find and Replace Text...

parameters.name: Check All Layers
parameters.description: Extend spell checking / replacement beyond the active layer.

parameters.name: Case Sensitive / Whole Word Only / Forward
parameters.description: Find and Replace options.

tools.example: Edit > Find and Replace Text: Find '2025', Change To '2026', tick Search All Layers, Change All.
tools.notes: Scripts can replace text via `textItem.contents` per layer; for many files use a Batch action containing Find and Replace Text.
